1.explanation:
1) RadioButton.js: This is where the readOnly prop must be accepted, forwarded to the <input>, and used to apply a new `bx--radio-button--readonly` class (or similar) on the wrapper or input to match the design tokens shown in the images. Without changes here, the component never renders any visual difference for read-only.
2) RadioButton.stories.js: We need to add a default `ReadOnly` story and include a `readOnly` control in the Playground args so designers and devs can preview and copy/paste the read-only variant.
3) RadioButton-test.js: There must be RTL unit tests asserting that the readOnly prop adds the correct class on the outer element and that the input has the readOnly attribute. These tests are missing.
4) RadioButton-test.e2e.js: The end-to-end snapshots should cover the read-only state (`components-radiobutton--read-only`) to catch any visual regressions in CI. Currently only the default (enabled) variant is captured.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots show the design guidelines for a read-only RadioButton: unselected, selected, and grouped states with specific color tokens and spacing for both vertical and horizontal layouts. The bug manifests because although the RadioButton component accepts a readOnly prop, there is no styling or markup in the component to visually indicate or enforce a read-only state—and there are no stories or tests covering it. Users expecting a non-editable, read-only radio button still see and can interact with the standard enabled component.
